summary.tldr: Requires the Public Safety minister to maintain and update Canada’s anti-human trafficking strategy, with regular reviews, reports and set measures.
what_it_does: Requires the Minister of Public Safety and Emergency Preparedness to maintain and update the National Strategy to Combat Human Trafficking.

Requires the strategy to include measures to support trafficked people, prevent trafficking, protect vulnerable groups, improve criminal justice responses, expand cooperation, create a website, train federal employees and track progress.
Requires the minister to try to make the strategy meet Canada’s obligations under four listed international agreements on women’s and children’s rights.
Requires a review of the strategy within two years and every five years after that, with public comments and consultations, and a report tabled in Parliament.
Requires the minister to publish the review report online 10 days after tabling it and to table an annual report on implementation within three months after each fiscal year.
summary.background: The bill creates a legal duty to maintain the National Strategy to Combat Human Trafficking. It defines human trafficking by reference to offences in the Criminal Code.
